Case Study · Fintech · Data Product

Databook: one place to read a company, instead of ten.

A unified financial intelligence platform that pulls a company's profile, directors, financials, charges, credit ratings and shareholding into a single, high-density workspace built for analysts, lenders and credit teams.

RoleDesign Lead
CompanyAccumn — A Yubi Company
DomainCredit & risk intelligence
ScopeIA, UI, design system
01 — The challenge

Company data is scattered by nature. The product shouldn't be.

Understanding a single company for a lending or risk decision means pulling from registrar filings, credit bureaus, exchanges, and internal notes — each with its own shape. The job was to bring that into one coherent product without flattening the depth analysts actually need.

Volume

Dozens of data points per entity

Profile, directors, charges, ratings, shareholding and compliance each carry their own dense tables and fields — every one needed at some point in a real decision.

Trust

Numbers have to be checkable

Ratings, charge amounts and shareholding percentages are only useful if their source and as-on date are always visible next to the figure.

Speed

Time-to-answer matters

Analysts move between many companies a day. Every extra click to confirm a fact is a click multiplied across a full workload.

02 — Approach

Three decisions that shaped the product.

01

One consistent entity shell

Every company page opens on the same shell — name, status, tags, and a fixed left-hand module list (Flags, Profile, Directors, Charges, Rating, Financials, Shareholding...). Once someone learns the shell on one company, it holds for all 130M+ entities in the system.

02

Structured cards over dense paragraphs

The profile view breaks company details, "about the company," important dates and contact information into distinct cards instead of one long form — so a user can scan the one card they need instead of reading the page top to bottom.

03

Filterable tables for anything repeating

Directors, charges and ratings are lists that grow over a company's lifetime. Each table carries per-column filters and sort, so "show me only open charges" or "only this rating agency" is a filter, not a scroll.

03 — Inside the product

A walk through the modules.

Six core modules from the shipped product, each solving a different shape of financial data.

Module 01

Profile

Company details, incorporation data and contact information are split into three cards side by side, so identity facts, narrative context and reach-out details never compete for the same line of sight.

Module 02

Directors

A dense, sortable register of every director — DIN, address, designation, stake held and contact — with column-level filters so a user can isolate, say, every promoter director without reading the full list.

Module 03

Flags & risk

Probability of default and degree of credit risk are translated into a single labelled gradient bar rather than a raw percentage, so risk reads at a glance before a user drills into the underlying event categories below it.

Module 04

Rating

Every historical rating action — agency, outlook, instrument, amount and action — sits in one paginated table, letting a 33-entry rating history stay readable instead of forcing a scroll through years of records.

Module 05

Shareholding

A promoter vs non-promoter donut sits next to a quarter-over-quarter breakdown table, pairing the at-a-glance shape of ownership with the exact numbers a diligence workflow needs to cite.

Module 06

Charges

Open versus closed charges are colour-coded down the left edge of each row, so scanning a long charges register for what's still live doesn't require reading every date column.

04 — Outcome

Source-reported impact.

38%lower cognitive load for first-time Databook users
30%faster, more consistent delivery from the shared design system
